summary: Modern databases and data platforms are increasingly embedding AI/ML capabilities natively, ranging from SQL-callable LLM functions and in-database model training to vector storage and similarity search. A key industry shift is the rise of PostgreSQL (with pgvector) as a general-purpose AI data layer, which, alongside object storage like Amazon S3 storing vectors, is narrowing but not eliminating the use cases for purpose-built vector databases such as Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant, and Weaviate. Despite heavy enterprise investment, many AI projects still fall short of ROI expectations, with data quality cited as the primary bottleneck.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst)
databases.description: Cortex is Snowflake's fully managed AI layer offering serverless SQL/Python-callable functions for text completion, summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, and embeddings using hosted foundation models (e.g., from Anthropic, Mistral, Meta, and Snowflake Arctic). It also powers semantic/RAG-style retrieval and can now extend to Snowflake Postgres environments via Cortex AI functions.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake provides a VECTOR data type and built-in vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.), plus Cortex Search as a managed hybrid vector+keyword retrieval service.
databases.llm_integration: Native hosted LLMs via Cortex COMPLETE and related functions; integrates Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, and Snowflake Arctic models without leaving the platform.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex AI functions billed by tokens processed / compute credits on top of standard Snowflake warehouse usage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-SQL model training) + Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run machine learning models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization) directly using SQL. It integrates tightly with Vertex AI to call hosted generative models (Gemini), generate embeddings, and run inference via remote models from within BigQuery.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR_SEARCH function and vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.llm_integration: Native via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and remote models backed by Vertex AI Gemini models and text-embedding endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: On-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based (slots) pricing; Vertex AI model calls and embedding generation billed separately through Vertex AI.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector adds vector data types and similarity operators to open-source PostgreSQL, enabling embedding storage and ANN search. The pgai extension brings LLM and embedding workflows into SQL (calling OpenAI, Ollama, and others), and pgvectorscale improves index performance, positioning Postgres as a leading general-purpose AI database in 2026.
databases.vector_search_notes: Via extension. Core PostgreSQL has no built-in vector search; it is added through the pgvector extension (with HNSW/IVFFlat indexes). Because it is an official, widely-adopted extension rather than a bundled core feature, capability depends on the extension being installed and enabled.
databases.llm_integration: Through the pgai extension, which exposes SQL functions to generate embeddings and call LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama, etc.) from within the database.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs come from the hosting provider or managed service (e.g., Timescale/Tiger, Supabase, Neon) running Postgres.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL-based inference via SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL functions that call out to Amazon SageMaker (custom models), Amazon Bedrock (foundation/generative models), and Amazon Comprehend (sentiment/NLP), without requiring ML expertise or moving data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided via the separate pgvector extension, not as a built-in feature of the Aurora ML service.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models (and SageMaker-hosted models) invoked directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/IO pricing; external SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend calls are billed separately by those services.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse model training and inference via SQL)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables creating, training, and deploying machine learning models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements, leveraging Amazon SageMaker (including Autopilot) under the hood. It also supports bringing in pre-trained models and invoking generative/LLM capabilities through integration with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift ML does not provide native vector similarity search as a core feature of the service. Redshift supports storage of vectors and some HNSW-style capabilities have emerged, but vector search is not the focus of Redshift ML and is not a native built-in of this service.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker to call LLMs and generative models from SQL (e.g., for text generation and embeddings).
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute (RPU/node) and storage pricing; SageMaker training and Bedrock inference billed separately through those services.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides a full lakehouse-native AI platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing models and GenAI agents, including foundation model APIs and RAG tooling. Databricks Vector Search delivers a managed, serverless vector database integrated with Unity Catalog governance and Delta tables.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed vector index that automatically syncs with Delta tables and supports hybrid (vector + keyword) search.
databases.llm_integration: Native via Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs (hosting Llama, DBRX, and external models like OpenAI/Anthropic) with RAG and agent frameworks.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based DBUs for compute, model serving, and vector search; serverless pricing varies by workload and region.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector search within MongoDB Atlas)
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores embeddings alongside operational document data and performs approximate nearest-neighbor search using HNSW indexes, enabling RAG and semantic search without a separate vector store. It integrates with Atlas Search for hybrid full-text + vector retrieval.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is a built-in Atlas feature using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage and dedicated vector search indexes, keeping vectors next to operational data.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs; integrates via application frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex) to generate embeddings and power RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing; Search Nodes can be provisioned separately for dedicated vector/search workloads, billed by node resources.
